MINUTES
  MEETING OF THE SAN MARINO
  LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES
  MONDAY FEBRUARY 28, 2022 AT 8:00 A.M.
  VIA TELECONFERENCE

CALL TO ORDER: Chairperson Domier called the meeting to order at 8:02 a.m. via
teleconference.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Chairperson Domier led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL:  PRESENT: Chairperson Steve Domier, Vice Chairperson Liz Hollingsworth,
  Trustee Linda Mollno, Trustee Lois Derry, Trustee Genevieve Chien, and
  Council Member Ken Ude

  ABSENT: None

  CITY STAFF PRESENT: Community Services Director Cathi Johnson,
  City Librarian Linda Vera, and Management Analyst Kristin Shigenaga

PUBLIC COMMENTS

The following person(s) provided comment:
  - None

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

1. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth moved, seconded by Trustee Chien, to approve the minutes of the
Library Board of Trustees meeting of Monday, January 24, 2022.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Chairperson Domier, Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth, Trustee Chien
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  Trustee Mollno
ABSENT:  Trustee Derry

Trustee Derry experienced technical issues with her microphone starting at 8:05 a.m. and was
  unable to fix the issue throughout the meeting.

BOARD OF TRUSTEES REPORTS

2. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Domier shared that he thinks 2022 has gotten off to a great start with the addition of
several new personnel, the work to fill the remaining Board member positions, and the newly revised
Donations Monitor. He is looking forward to continuing the progress throughout the year.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 2 OF 10

3. TRUSTEE REPORTS

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth shared that she met virtually with Management Analyst Shigenaga
last week. She appreciates Management Analyst Shigenaga’s work on the new Budget and Donations
Monitors as well as the inclusion of photos of the Bookmark contest winners and the number of program
participants in the Director and City Librarian’s report.

Trustee Chien, Trustee Mollno, and Trustee Derry did not have anything to report at this time.

4. CRAIN ART GALLERY REPORT

Trustee Mollno shared that January and February’s exhibit displayed local watercolor artist, Marie
McDuffie. McDuffie’s theme was local places in San Marino and the surrounding area. Her reception
was cancelled due to the pandemic, but quite a few people still came anyways. The artist sold over
half of her paintings and will be sending over a donation to the Library.
Trustee Mollno shared that there is a little cabinet in the hallway known as the “Trustees’ Cabinet.”
Lynda Lyons of the Crain Art Gallery Committee is in charge of scheduling what goes in the Cabinet.
While McDuffie’s artwork was on display, her sketch book was in the Cabinet to show any non-
artists what a sketch book looks like. In addition to the sketch books, there were also some art
palettes and tools in there, which Trustee Mollno thought were really nice additions to the paintings.
The next exhibit begins on March 9 and will display works by Verdugo Hills Artist Association. It
will be a juried exhibit, which means artists submit paintings and then the juror, Pete Morris from
Los Angeles County, picks the paintings to be included. The title of the exhibit will be Art and
Artistry and there will most likely be no reception.
The following exhibit will display April Drew Foster’s work from April 23 to June 3. Foster had
virtual exhibit in the Gallery during the pandemic, and has been offered an in-person exhibit now
that the Library is open again. There will a reception either at the Library or at her home. The
preferred location for the reception is the Library, since receptions are usually when artists sell
most of their artwork. Director Johnson shared that the Committee can count on that reception
occurring in person at the Library in April.
Trustee Mollno explained that the summer months have not yet been booked with artists. The
September and October exhibit will most likely feature a group called The Plein Airs. One of the
group members, Susan Culter, has already submitted some of the works. The November and
December exhibit will most likely feature Trustee Mollno.
The Crain Art Gallery was established in 2009 as a tribute to former City Librarian, Carolyn Crain,
with restricted donations designated specifically for its formation and maintenance. The Gallery has
its own budget line items. The current Budget Monitor shows a balance of $12,427. Since then, there
has been a donation of $370 from the November/December artist, which will show up on the next
Monitor.
In 2018, the Board worked very hard to resolve the issue of the missing donations. Based off the
Minutes from the January 2022 meeting, Trustee Mollno thinks that the issue has been resolved. She
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 3 OF 10

shared that tracking of donations is a recurring concern of the Gallery Committee since there was
a time when they thought their donations had been lost and lumped into the General Fund. The
income for the Gallery is mostly from a voluntary 20% donation from the artists, which is low
compared to the requirements of other galleries. Expenses are relatively light and usually just include
lightbulbs and postage, but there may come a time when more costly expenses may come up. The
income should cover for rainy days without needing support from the City.
The current Committee includes: Lynda Lyons, Library Staff; Sandy Morris, former Trustee; Debra
Sadun, Library Foundation Representative; Linda Mollno, Trustee; and Rosa Zee, former School
District member and current President of the Chinese Floral Arts Association. Eva Margueriette has
recently stepped down from the Committee and the process has begun to replace her.
Trustee Mollno shared that her term ends in May and asked Chairperson Domier to begin the
discussion to see who will become the new liaison to the Committee. She explained that it is likely
that she will stay on the Committee and fill in the open position.
Trustee Mollno pointed out that Marie McDuffie’s exhibit needed to be taken down and rehung due
to the unannounced painting of the Library. She shared that open communication needs to occur so
this doesn’t happen. Director Johnson and City Librarian Vera explained that the painting crew
started to work ahead of schedule without communicating to Staff which areas would be worked
on that day. They apologized for the inconvenience.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth thanked Trustee Mollno for being a representative to the Crain
Art Gallery. She encouraged Trustee Mollno to spend the donation money in the reserves, as the
City should help with facilities enhancement if needed.
Trustee Mollno asked Director Johnson about the permit application from Los Angeles County to
serve food at events in Library facilities. Director Johnson responded that the City follows the Los
Angeles County Department of Public Health guidelines for serving refreshments and this is not a
new requirement; Library Staff might not have been aware of it previously. Trustee Mollno asked
that this policy be shared with anyone interested in using the space. City Librarian Vera noted that
in library settings, prepackaged food items are usually provided, so a permit is not required. Director
Johnson tasked City Librarian Vera to provide the guidelines to the Trustees and others who will
use City facilities. Chairperson Domier asked if the group renting the area or the Library is
responsible for obtaining the permit and Director Johnson responded that it depends on if it is a
City-sponsored event or a private rental. Trustee Mollno requested that the guidelines include how
far in advance the permit needs to be applied for.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth agreed with City Librarian Vera’s comment that providing
prepackaged refreshments might be the best option for receptions.
Chairperson Domier thanked Trustee Mollno for the detailed report of the Crain Art Gallery.

5. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

Chairperson Domier reported that he was unable to attend the last meeting. He asked Council
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 4 OF 10

Member Ude to provide an update.

Council Member Ude shared that the remodel of San Marino Center (SMC) is supposed to make it
look like the Library, but the City learned that they cannot change the outside look. This then
required the architect to redo the design of the exterior, which is in process, and then it will it go
out to bid. Public Works Director Throne prescreened some contractors and the goal is to have
shovels in the ground by the 4th quarter of this year, assuming the project gets approved. The next
step is reviewing the final quotes from the prescreened contractors. Chairperson Domier asked if
it is possible for the two buildings to look similar from the back side? Council Member Ude
responded that this can be discussed with the architect.

Trustee Mollno shared that her husband has an office building in Pasadena, which is registered as a
historic site. Her husband wanted to remodel it and Pasadena’s only requirement was to keep the
front of the building the same. She suggested Council Member Ude to look closely to the
registration, where it comes from, and the parameters.

ADMINISTRATIVE BUSINESS

6. DIRECTOR AND CITY LIBRARIAN REPORT

Director Johnson presented the Director and City Librarian Report. The recruitment for the full-
time Adult Services Librarian II was not successful; the two final candidates declined the offer. Youth
Services Librarian is on maternity leave, so City Librarian Vera and Circulation Librarian Plumley are
doing double duty, as the Library is operating with two out of four full time librarians. Director
Johnson complimented City Librarian Vera for managing the Library with limited capacity as the
Library continues to get busier. City Librarian Vera added that she is excited to get the right person
in who will complement the team and do a great job. Chairperson Domier shared that other
employers have the same difficulty recruiting. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth agreed that waiting
for the right person is key and asked if the Library has any substitutes on hand to help out in the
time being. City Librarian Vera explained that the Library is not relying on substitutes; instead, she
schedules flexibly and creatively with the resources available. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth
encourages City Librarian Vera to find a list of substitutes because two people doing four jobs is too
much.

Director Johnson shared the fiscal year 2022-23 CIP and Operating Budget Development Calendar,
which comes from the City Manager and Finance Director. She explained that the Board will get an
opportunity to review the Library’s operating budget and CIP submissions, prior to the April 22 City
Council meeting. In order to have feedback from the City Manager and Finance Director before
presenting in to the Board, she requested the Board forego the March 28 meeting and instead meet
on April 11.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked why March 28 doesn’t work. Director Johnson explained
that Staff meet with the City Manager on March 30 and 31. In order to have enough time to get the
packet ready, the presentation to the Board needs to be on April 11. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth agreed forego the March 28 meeting, but would like to keep April 25 meeting on the
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 5 OF 10

calendar. She thinks that the Board should decide on April 11 if the April 25 meeting is needed or
not.
The Board agreed to advise Staff to cancel the March 28 meeting, call a special meeting on April 11,
and keep the April 25 meeting on the calendar.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if the March 9 joint City Council meeting is still occurring.
Director Johnson shared that the meeting has moved to the fall, with no official date yet, per the
City Manager.
Director Johnson asked if there were any questions on the Budget or Donations Monitor.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth shared that she appreciates Management Analyst Shigenaga’s notes
in comments section, which helps the Board better understand the budget. She asked how the
Library will spend $18,000 from the Friends. Management Analyst Shigenaga responded that this was
discussed with Finance Director Paul Chung, as current Staff were not here when the budget was
developed. Director Chung explained that prior Staff budgeted expenses expecting to dip into the
Reserves, explaining why expenditures are higher than revenue for the fiscal year.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth shared that she talked to Management Analyst Shigenaga about
designated and undesignated funds. There are not a lot of donations that are designated, so the goal
is to look for the 5 or 6 designated donations that were carried across years to verify that the
money is spent the way the donor requested. She shared that if the Library spends the money,
tracking the donations year over year won’t be necessary. She requested Staff to come up with new
ideas for spending the reserves. Director Johnson noted that the Library needs staff in order to be
able to spend money.
Director Johnson then moved onto the operational updates. She explained on February 25, the
Department of Public Health came out with a new order easing the masking mandate. The City is
required to set up checkpoints at all facilities, including the Library and Friends Book Shoppe to ask
for proof of vaccination if they’d like to unmask. She shared that Staff have professional protocol
and scripts ready to have this conversation with patrons. Adjustments will be made as needed.
Chairperson Domier asked if there will be any signage in Book Shoppe. Director Johnson clarified
that the checkpoint will catch people before they enter the Book Shoppe and new signage will be
coming.
Trustee Chien asked if proof of vaccination includes 1 shot, 2 shots, or 3 shots? City Librarian Vera
responded that the definition of fully vaccination does not include the booster shot. Director
Johnson added that the City is following the guidelines from the Department of Public Health.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked how this will impact bringing back various volunteers.
Director Johnson responded that if they volunteer for the City, they fall under the City volunteer
policy and they have to be fully vaccinated.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 6 OF 10

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if this is going to bring the Board closer to resuming in-
person Trustee meetings. Director Johnson responded that it is a City Council decision and that
she will check with the City Manager.
Director Johnson shared that Community Services is going to be featured on the next virtual Town
Hall on March 7 at 6 PM. She encouraged all to attend virtually.
She shared that the Board recruitment update information came from the City Clerk. The City
Clerk is reviewing an ordinance on the March 9 City Council meeting. Director Johnson encouraged
the Board to attend that meeting to learn firsthand knowledge regarding the City’s boards and
commissions.
Trustee Mollno expressed her frustration with the number of times that the Board has been told
this same information over the last year. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth suggested that the Board
recruitment be an agenda item on the April 25 meeting so Director Johnson can report on what
was decided at the March City Council meeting. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth explained that in
the past, when the Board has had strong feelings about something, the Chairperson or Vice
Chairperson emailed the City Council to express the Board’s thoughts. She recommended
Chairperson Domier email City Council to be quick and diligent for all board and commission
recruitments. Chairperson Domier agreed that is a good idea. Trustee Mollno, Trustee Chien, and
Trustee Derry expressed their support for the email to be sent to City Council.
Director Johnson continued to explain that the major update from the Foundation was about the
Bookmark contest, as they did not meet in February.
City Librarian Vera shared that the Library transitioned programming from indoors to outdoors.
The Huntington Nurses would like to bring on a second nurse, which she thinks supports the
Library’s mission of supporting a certain quality of life. She emphasized that the Library is a place for
all informational needs and program development is done with care and forethought to encourage
creativity, curiosity, and lifelong learning. Director Johnson added that the passport program is in
very high demand and revenue is expected to exceed the budgeted amount. Passport acceptance
services are by appointment only and additional staff are being trained to be able to support this
service.
Director Johnson shared that there are two Public Works projects. The painting project is complete
for the most part and the targeted completion date for StoryWalk at Lacy Park is May. The kickoff
is targeted for the end of May.
Director Johnson explained that Community Services Staff have been able to put efforts into being
active on social media through Facebook and Instagram. The followers on Facebook saw an increase
of 6% and 1% on Instagram.
Trustee Mollno noted the difference between the number of people who like a post and the number
of people who participate in the program. She requested that the Library not rely on social media
for spreading the word about programs and events; she would like to see press releases with the
same information in the San Marino Tribune or Pasadena Star News on a monthly basis.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 7 OF 10

Director Johnson commented that the Library would love to be more proactive and announce
upcoming programing, but lack the staff to do so. She shared that her goal was to get this position
for the Department, but was told no new positions. As a result, the Department relies upon the
City Hall marketing and communication staff. She explained that she believes the staff will try to
assist with press releases upon request. Director Johnson added that she could not agree more with
Trustee Mollno’s request for press releases; she explained that she would love to push out one
press release a month, but the Department has been in reacting mode due to staffing gaps.
Trustee Mollno suggested that any articles mentioning the Library be included in the Director’s
Report, even if it isn’t a Staff driven article. Director Johnson agreed and noted that she will have
staff look out for any local news regarding the Library.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth shared that she thinks one of the important ways to get the word
out to the whole community is through the school newsletters, particularly Carver and Valentine.
She recommended that a staff member be assigned to email the schools to request that an
advertisement be included in the newsletter. She asked several questions about StoryWalk.
Director Johnson shared that she will work with City Librarian Vera on the marketing campaign for
StoryWalk. She then responded to Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth’s comment about delegating the
duty and responsibility to an existing staff member. She shared that there is no one with that level
of duty and responsibility within their job description. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth
recommended getting some substitutes to assist with this. She then requested that the plans for
StoryWalk and Summer Reading Club be an agenda item at the April meeting, as she has several
questions about both.
City Librarian Vera shared that she is the only one buying books for Adult and Children’s and
planning this program. She asked Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth if there is anything in particular
that she is concerned with. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth requested a report on various details
related to the summer reading program. Director Johnson noted an update on program plans will
be provided at the next meeting.
Chairperson Domier asked if it would be helpful if Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth sends all the
suggestions to City Librarian Linda? City Librarian Vera noted that she has run similar programs for
several years now and understands that clarity is desired on everything. Trustee Mollno offered to
meet with City Librarian Vera to provide historical background of what the Library had done in the
past with this program. Director Johnson noted that Youth Services Librarian has been handling this
program and can be reached if City Librarian Vera needs help. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth
shared that she can help with the outreach and search for student volunteers.
Chairperson Domier highlighted that two Board members will be leaving soon and that Staff should
take advantage of their willingness to volunteer and share knowledge.
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 8 OF 10

NEW BUSINESS

7. DISCUSSION OF FY 22-23 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PLAN PROJECTS

Director Johnson shared the Staff Report includes three projects that will be considered through
this year’s budget process. The first project is the computer room renovation which is slated for FY
2022-23 at $25,000. This project will be funded by a donation from Foundation. The other two
items are the security camera system and the Barth Community Room audio/visual upgrade. She
shared that the Public Works Director and City Manager oversee the CIP plan for the City. She
highlighted the security camera system will be bundled, as part of a citywide security camera system,
that will be bid and led by the Public Works Director. Similarly, the Barth Community Room
audio/visual upgrade will be bundled with the San Marino Center to allow for similar equipment and
vendors.
Trustee Mollno asked what will happen with the audio/visual upgrade if the San Marino Center
project does not go through. Director Johnson responded that she would communicate to Public
Works Director and the City Manager that the need is still there and Staff would like it to still be
considered as a standalone project.
Trustee Mollno shared that this budget request originated before the pandemic as a standalone item.
Once the renovation of San Marino Center came about, the bundling idea made sense. She is just
worried that the community as whole doesn’t support the renovation, and doesn’t want the Library
to suffer as a result of not being able to use Barth Room.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth added that this item was brought forward by City Council liaisons
2-3 years ago to allow for City Council to have their meetings in Barth Room during the San Marino
Center renovation. There was also a lighting upgrade request for the same room. She suggested to
move the project from FY 2023-24 to FY 2022-23. Trustee Mollno agreed. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth clarified that she would like to move the project up in the timeline since the upgrades
are needed to support rental groups and to have it done before the San Marino Center renovation.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that StoryWalk is not listed and asked if it is omitted because
it is funded. Director Johnson responded that StoryWalk was part of the operating budget.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth asked Management Analyst Shigenaga to screenshare the list of
projects from March 9, 2020. She shared how exciting it is to see how many projects have been
completed. Management Analyst Shigenaga asked what the Thornton Room display is and Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth responded that it is not a projector; instead, it is a large flat screen
monitor. Director Johnson responded that this expense would be included in the operating budget.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth suggested Staff maintain a list of incomplete projects or operational
maintenance requests so everyone can know the direction the Library is moving towards and donors
know how they can support. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth requested the Barth Room A/V
upgrade move to FY 2022-23 and that the Barth Room lighting project be added. Trustee Mollno
shared her agreement and supports anything that can be done without going through the CIP
 LIBRARY BOARD OF TRUSTEES MINUTES  REGULAR MEETING
FEBRUARY 28, 2022  PAGE 9 OF 10

process. Trustee Chien agreed with Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth. She has noticed projects
dragging on during her time on the Board.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth commented that there is $62,000 in the reserve account for the
Library to spend. City Librarian Vera thanked Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth for providing so much
background knowledge.
Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth moved, seconded by Trustee Mollno, to have Staff update the
Capital Priority List and place it on the May agenda, move the Barth Community Room A/V project
to FY 2022-23, and for the Chairperson or Vice Chairperson to email the City Council that the
Board has consensus with the CIP proposed by Staff and that the Board would like the Barth Room
A/V project moved up to FY 2022-23.

Motion passed by the following vote:

AYES:  Chairperson Domier, Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth, Trustee Chien, Trustee
  Mollno
NOES:  None
ABSTAIN:  None
ABSENT:  Trustee Derry

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth acknowledged that the Capital Priority list has items that have not
been completed, which is understandable due to COVID-19, but others are not understandable.
Chairperson Domier added that waiting until San Marino Center is renovated before upgrading the
A/V is an unnecessarily long wait. The upgrade needs to happen so that it can be used when the San
Marino Center undergoes construction.

8. DISCUSSION OF POSSIBLE BOARD LIAISON ROLES TO THE FRIENDS OF
  THE CROWELL PUBLIC LIBRARY AND SAN MARINO PUBLIC LIBRARY
  FOUNDATION

Chairperson Domier shared that the goal is to have one Board Member be a liaison to the San
Marino Public Library Foundation and one to the Friends of the Crowell Public Library to form
stronger bonds between the three support groups.
Trustee Mollno shared that the Library can only benefit by the three support groups working
together. She would be happy to be liaison to the Friends.
Vice Chair Hollingsworth agreed that it is a great idea. She proposed another option of inviting
Foundation and Friends representations to the quarterly financial meetings.
Trustee Chien asked if the Board should wait to assign liaison roles until the two new members are
onboarded. Chairperson Domier responded that he thinks the Board should fill the liaison roles
now, so that new members will have some guidance if stepping into the liaison roles.
